description: Global vertex connectivity through vertex splitting and repeated augmenting-path max flow.

source.title: Edge connectivity / Vertex connectivity
source.license_note: The article's license applies to its text. This package uses its high-level algorithm description only; no article prose, code, or test data is reproduced.

input.graph_semantics: undirected simple graph; duplicate edges are coalesced and self-loops are ignored
input.definition: Disconnected graphs have connectivity 0; a complete graph on n>=2 vertices has connectivity n-1; otherwise the result is the minimum number of vertices whose removal disconnects the graph.

contract.method: For each nonadjacent vertex pair, split each graph vertex into an in/out pair, cap internal split arcs at one and graph arcs at one, then compute an augmenting-path maximum flow. The minimum pairwise flow is global vertex connectivity; complete graphs return n-1.
contract.complexity: O(V^2) max-flow calls in the worst case, each using bounded Edmonds-Karp on a 2V-node split graph; the local profile caps V at 10 and E at 45.
contract.distinctness: Computes arbitrary vertex-separator cardinality, beyond articulation-point (single-vertex cut) detection; this is not edge connectivity or global edge min-cut.

workspace.meaning: 10 adjacency masks, a 10-element fixed-array helper copy on Zig, 20x20 residual capacities, and graph/BFS queue and parent arrays.
